== Update - August 26, 2026 ==

=== New items for sale ===

==== The Purveyor [Bonus Merchant] ====

[[The Purveyor]] [Bonus Merchant] is a new merchant in [[Ascalon City (pre-Searing)|Ascalon City]], [[Lion's Arch]], [[Kaineng Center]], [[Kamadan]], and the [[Great Temple of Balthazar]]. The Purveyor buys and sells some normal items, but also provides access to new account upgrades that are purchasable through the in-game store or via the Guild Wars web store.

* Infinite Identification and Salvage Kit Bundle - $9.99 USD - If you have this account upgrade, the Purveyor will provide you Infinite Identification and Infinite Salvage kits. Both items never run out of charges.
* Merchant Summoning Item - Purveyor's Bell - $6.99 USD - If you have this account upgrade, the Purveyor will provide you the [[Purveyor's Bell]], which allows you to summon the Purveyor in any explorable area, giving you access to merchant services out in the field. With this upgrade, the Purveyor will provide you a [[Reforged Coin]] once daily, which is redeemable with the Purveyor for a variety of useful items (items redeemable with Reforged Coins are subject to change).

==== Account upgrade bundles ====

Two new account upgrade bundles are purchasable through the in-game store or via the Guild Wars web store.

* Reforged Starter Bundle - $14.99 USD - Adds two additional [[Character slot|character slots]] and two additional [[Xunlai Storage Pane|storage panes]] in the [[Vault box|Xunlai storage chest]].
* Reforged Costume Bundle - $29.99 USD - Unlocks all purchasable [[Costume|costumes]] that exist so far!
:: You must own less than 9 existing costumes.

=== Cartographer title tuning changes ===

The cartographer title has had difficult edge cases since it launched.  We've been working on the balance of it to make it more accessible while retaining the challenge of completely exploring maps.  In this release, we've modified the calculation of 'completeness' to account for the very difficult to uncover map tiles that exist in some maps.  We intend to sell this item in the future and it will be identical to the version that is dropped in-game.  Before we sell it in the shop we want it dialed in as best as we can.

=== Skill balance pass philosophy ===

The August update features over 150 skill changes across all ten professions. Here's the philosophy that went into today's update.

We continue to try to highlight underutilized skills with real potential to increase build versatility, flexibility, and variety. We saw some encouraging movement in our key metrics for skill usage after the June update and we are looking to build on that while adjusting some skills that were pushed into over/under-powered territory.

For PvE casual and speedclear players, our high-level goal is driving interesting varieties of viable builds with the potential for fun new discoveries.  This increases as underutilized skills become increasingly viable. We also want the meta builds reasonable and not too powerful/dominant which would trivialize content.

For PvP our goal is to tone down dominant builds until we get into an interesting meta rotation where there are no "best at everything" builds that cannot be countered. We want players to constantly be coming up with clever ways to use the massive set of skills to keep their opponents on their toes.

Most of this update is focused on buffs—cheaper costs, faster recharges, and quality-of-life improvements—aimed at skills and attribute lines that are not seeing much play. When we do nerf a skill, we are targeting specific skills that are suppressing build creativity. They do so by creating strategies so dominant that it doesn't make sense to use anything else.  In the case of PvP, there isn't compelling counterplay. When we make those adjustments, they are targeted at the environment where the problem actually lives (PvE or PvP generally). There are also several skills that have seen significant functionality rework to increase the  spectrum of builds.  Some of the changes create a more clear identity for those skills while reinforcing the core profession fantasy.

We're incredibly grateful to the community for providing a wealth of excellent feedback and detailed notes/suggestions after the June balance patch and we look forward to seeing what y'all think about this one!

We try to keep the update notes as accurate as possible, but we are live updating these skills based on testing and sometimes miss updating the notes.  We love reading your notes on the build.  We can make emergency adjustments where they are needed with small hotfixes, but generally we are going to let the meta play out for a while to see where further adjustments are needed.

That said, this is likely to be last really big balance update this year.

=== Other adjustments ===

* [[Costume maker]] and [[Shrine to Godly Accoutrements]] are now available in [[Ascalon City]].

==== Skill bug fixes ====

* {{skill icon|Ebon Hawk}} - Fix an issue where Weakness was being applied for 20 seconds regardless of the caster's Earth attribute, now appropriately scales based on the attribute.
* {{skill icon|Renewing Surge}} - Hex correctly triggers its end effect when the target dies.
* {{skill icon|Sand Shards}} - Recasting while the enchantment is already active correctly refreshes the number of strikes.

==== Skill AI adjustments ====

* {{skill icon|Splinter Weapon}} - Casters target allies again, but only if they are in range AND in your team display (NPC allies), minions, pets, and summons. Party is prioritized first.
* {{skill icon|Strength of Honor}} - Casters no longer drop a third maintained enchantment instantly and can sustain this on 3 melee characters. No longer drop the enchant if weapon is changed from melee.

==== Pet AI adjustments ====

* [[Animal companion|Pets]] in guard no longer attack close-range [[target]]s unless the targets are hostile.
* Pets in guard no longer automatically attack their player's target unless the player calls the target or sets it as a locked target.
* Pets in guard updated targeting priority: 1. Locked target 2. Called target 3. AI choice.
* Increased responsiveness when a higher-priority target is set by the player.

=== Known issues ===

* Several skills received updated text after our localization deadline and are missing localized text. These will be fixed in our next localization pass.

=== Skill update details ===

==== [[Assassin]] ====

Sharpen the opportunist identity of the profession—deadly against isolated targets, unmatched mobility, in and out before anyone knows you were there. Utility and lead-in attack tools are generally cheaper and several projectiles have been sped up to make hitting more consistent, so ambush and split play cost less to attempt. In exchange, PvP versions of a couple of mobility and shutdown outliers now ask for real investment—incredible mobility should be a significant part of your build choice, not a freebie.

* {{skill icon|Disrupting Dagger}} - Double projectile speed.
* {{skill icon|Expunge Enchantments}} - Reduce skill disable from 10..5 to 8..4.
* {{skill icon|Mantis Touch}} - Reduce recharge from 20 to 10.

==== [[Dervish]] ====

Still looking to rein in Dervishes a bit on the PvP side of things. The overall efficiency of many of their skills is significantly higher than other professions and the jack-of-all-trades nature of a lot of their kit makes counterplay frustrating (if it is possible at all). On the PvE side of things, we're working on a few buffs to open up some options and an overhaul to Mirage Cloak that retains its core identity while opening up interesting new synergies with other skills and professions.

* {{skill icon|Aura Slicer (PvP)}} - Split for PvP. Increase adrenaline cost from 4 to 5.
* {{skill icon|Fleeting Stability (PvP)}} - Split for PvP. Reduce duration from 4..10 to 2..8. (BOTH) Reduce recharge from 15 to 10.
* {{skill icon|Grenth's Grasp}} - Remove the cold-weapon requirement.
* {{skill icon|Harrier's Grasp (PvP)}} - Split for PvP. Rework: "(5..20 second[s].) Melee attacks on moving foes also Cripple them…".
* {{skill icon|Mirage Cloak}} - Increase energy cost from 10 to 15, increase duration from 1..7 to 20, increase recharge from 15 to 24, rework: "For 20 seconds, you have a 40% chance to block and an additional 10% for each enchantment (max 80%). Each time an enchantment is removed from you, all nearby foes are struck for 10..40 earth damage."

* {{skill icon|Mystic Corruption (PvP)}} - Split for PvP. Adjust Disease duration from 1..10 to 2..6.

* {{skill icon|Signet of Pious Restraint (PvP)}} - Increase recharge from 10 to 16.

==== [[Elementalist]] ====

Mainly looking to bring the Water attribute up with this update—with several skills getting adjustments to increase their utility in addition to generally being significantly cheaper and faster. On the Air front, a few of June's adjustments cut deeper than we wanted, so we are readjusting those to restore their overall efficiency. A couple of adjustments to energy managements skills rounds out the package along with the game's first new skill in a while. We are experimenting with a new—PvE-only—skill that gives players a new tool to manage Overcast in an interesting way. Our goal is to use this version of the skill for community testing to determine if it is viable for PvP as well. Please share your feedback on the skill as you figure out interesting builds with it.

==== [[Ranger]] ====
Reducing the super long-range spirits. The increase in their original distance was generally good, but it produced key frustrating situations—in PvP, spirits could influence fights from total safety and in PvE, enemy spirit effects were so large they were causing some unintended group crossover dynamics. The range is still increased from the original, but splitting the difference should tone down those frustrating, unintended situations. Some PvP adjustments to tone down a few build synergies that have been a bit too dominant in the recent meta. On the buff side of things, PvP rangers can now bring their pets along without having to take Charm Animal and there are some general buffs to bow attack skills.

==== [[Warrior]] ====
